questions.question: Under what condition is an implication p→q false?
alternatives: false only when antecedent true and consequent false
questions.explanation: An implication p→q is false only when the antecedent is true and consequent is false.

questions.question: What is the symbol for NAND?
What is the symbol for NOR?
What property allows an operator to express all other logical operators?
questions.explanation: NAND and NOR are functionally complete - they can create all other operators.

questions.question: What is another name for XOR?
questions.explanation: XOR (exclusive OR) excludes the case where both operands are true.

questions.question: Which binary operator is true exactly when its two operands have the same truth value?
questions.explanation: The biconditional p↔q is true when p and q share a truth value; AND and OR differ when operands differ.

questions.question: What is the precedence order for operators?
What is p⊕p (p XOR p) equivalent to?
questions.explanation: XOR is true only when operands differ; identical operands yield False.

questions.question: Using only two basic operators, p→q can be rewritten with which pair?
questions.explanation: p→q ≡ ¬p∨q, expressing implication via negation and disjunction.

questions.question: How is p NOR q written using OR and NOT?
questions.explanation: NOR negates the disjunction of its operands.

questions.question: What is the output of p NAND p?
questions.explanation: p NAND p = ¬(p∧p) = ¬p, so a NAND gate with tied inputs acts as NOT.

questions.question: Name a binary operator that is NOT associative.
questions.explanation: (p→q)→r differs from p→(q→r); NAND and NOR are also non-associative.
